# SQLucid: Grounding Natural Language Database Queries with Interactive Explanations

## Research question

Non-experts may accept a plausible but incorrect SQL result because they cannot inspect its computation or express a precise correction.

## Method

SQLucid combines grammar-based step explanations with linked table/column highlighting, intermediate results computed over the full database and editable explanation steps. SmBoP generates the initial SQL; STEPS converts edited descriptions into clause updates. Users can add, remove or revise steps and revisit edit history.

## Evaluation

A randomized-order within-subject study compares adapted MISP, DIY and SQLucid with a shared SmBoP backend in 30 university students. Each condition gives eight stratified Spider tasks and ten minutes. A second eight-person study ablates highlighting and intermediate results. Separately, the first author attempts 100 tasks.

## What the results support

Study 1 reports 85% correctness among completed tasks, while Figure 7 shows 70% of all assigned tasks correct. Participants complete 6.6 of eight tasks per session. The feature study favors the full interface; the separate author-operated trial reports 89%, not a novice-user result.

## Limits and qualifications

Skipped and unattempted tasks are excluded from the headline accuracy denominator. Student sampling, small ablation groups and adapted historical baselines limit generalization. Self-reported confidence is not calibrated correctness. Printed task/reference mismatches require checking before reuse; their effect on study scoring is unknown. Later ChatGPT-based code is not evaluated by this paper.

## Relevance to reliable Text-to-SQL

An adjacent human-verification and feedback interface with measured effort and repair outcomes. It supports inspecting and correcting generated SQL, without evaluating autonomous clarification decisions, refusal or complete ambiguity coverage.
